title: Capacity probation, smoothing and approval lattice for Dedicated reservations
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem statement: we need a defensible, repeatable workflow for Dedicated capacity reservations that balances customer throughput guarantees with limited fleet availability and cost discipline. Current intake is manual and leads to overcommitment during spikes. This ticket defines: 1) a probation window for new reservations, 2) a smoothing/band strategy to convert committed throughput into practical capacity allocations, and 3) an approval lattice that routes, grades, and escalates requests.

Scope and goals:
- Define probation defaults (72-hour soft-commit followed by full commit) and edge triggers for shortening/lengthening probation.
- Formalize smoothing: a three-band policy (committed, buffer, burst) with explicit formulas that map requested throughput to reserved GPU units and burst quotas.
- Design autoscaling policy templates for Dedicated: target-utilization (default 70%), min/max pool sizing, burst pool sizing, and cost caps.
- Approval lattice: self-serve quick-approve for low-risk requests, staged review for medium/high risk (finance + SRE), and manual exec sign-off for very large commitments.
- Operational controls: automatic probation telemetry, canary gating (gradual ramp), and automated decommit/adjust triggers if utilization < 40% over 10 days.

Key decisions so far:
- Probation default is 72 hours (Configurable per customer). Rationale: gives real workload signal while limiting long tail churn. Trade-off: may frustrate customers needing immediate hard guarantees; remedy with an expedited paid path handled by Sales/Finance.
- Smoothing bands: committed = 70% of requested throughput, buffer = +20% for predictable bursts, burst = +10% from a shared transient pool. Mapping to fleet units uses a cost-weighted token that accounts for model family (Llama3 vs Mistral) and quantization profile.
- Autoscale template: target_utilization=70, scale_cooldown=300s, max_scale_rate=2x/hour, burst_pool=15% of fleet by default. Trade-off: lower target utilization reduces unit cost efficiency but increases headroom for tail latency SLOs.

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle multi-tenant bursts that exceed shared burst pool? Proposed fallback: auto-fallback to lower-cost model variant + throttled queueing.
- Accounting for heterogenous model footprints when calculating GPU pool equivalents. Proposed approach: normalized token-cost model plus conservative rounding up for safety.
- Billing implications during probation: bill at committed rate but with pro-rated credits if probation de-escalates. Legal/finance to sign off.

Milestones and deliverables:
- Week 1: Formalize formulas and default parameters + Confluence spec (linked below).
- Week 2: Implement intake form changes and automated scoring (PoC in intake service).
- Week 3: Integrate telemetry and probation dashboard; add rollout canary for two pilot customers.
- Week 4: Finalize approval matrix and handoff to Sales/Finance/SRE for operational runbook.

Operational/runbook excerpts:
- Decommit rule: if utilization < 40% for 10 consecutive days, auto-create a decommit proposal for review.
- Escalation rule: customer requests > 5x current committed throughput trigger exec review.
- Canary ramp: 10% -> 33% -> 66% -> 100% over 72 hours unless anomaly triggers rollback.

- SRE to review auto-decommit thresholds for operational risk (owner: Priya Singh).
